afterDepthFixVisualJudgement.sameSeeding: Same script, same recipe: 74 buildings, 5 terrace blocks (blockCount=5), rerun end-to-end after the CSS-only depth fix (dev-team confirmed no grid-track/layout change, 103 tests still pass).
afterDepthFixVisualJudgement.steppedVsFlatVerdict: Real improvement, now reads as stepped, not just flat-with-tint. 09 shows 5 clearly distinct plateau tones block-to-block (pale pink -> warm tan/gold -> deeper gold -> peach -> pale mint), not the near-identical cream-on-cream of 07. 10 (1:1 closeup) shows a genuinely visible dark brown earth band between the upper plateau and the road — that band was nearly invisible in 08. This is the missing elevation cue named in the prior verdict; it now reads.
afterDepthFixVisualJudgement.toneCheck: Still pastel, not muddy. The added brown is confined to the earth strip at each terrace boundary — it doesn't spread into the plateau body or the buildings, and the buildings themselves (blue/purple/orange/teal/pink) keep the frame dominantly bright/pastel. Would flag as a concern only if the earth band creeps wider than one road row or the plateau tints keep pushing warmer — not the case here.
afterDepthFixVisualJudgement.roadAndNpcCheck: Road reads as a continuous grey ribbon with an unbroken dashed centerline in both 09 and 10 — the deeper (20px) earth band is not visibly painting over or breaking the road, consistent with TownGrid.tsx's DOM-order guarantee (cross-street renders after the terrace, road always on top). tallTown NPC placement check (checkNpcPlacement, same bbox-overlap method) rerun after the fix: all 12 NPCs still onRoad and insideGrid at 5-block scale (see afterDepthFixTallTownAllNpcsOnRoad/InsideGrid above) — no regression from the deeper earth band.
afterDepthFixVisualJudgement.remainingGap: Not re-litigating the props-layer gap (§5, already flagged as deliberately deferred, not blocking) — this judgement is scoped to the terrain-depth question only.

performance.note: Gap = wall-clock ms between detected npc-slot style changes, 100ms poll granularity, STEP_INTERVAL_MS=2500 is the expected floor. Terraces removed mid-run (DOM node reduction only, not a re-mount) to isolate terrain's paint/layout cost from the fixed 2500ms tick.

tallTownVisualJudgement.verdictDetail: At 07 (full-width, zoomed to fit, 5 blocks stacked), the town reads as tinted horizontal color bands separated by grey cross-streets — NOT as Fortune City-style stepped multi-level terrain. The tint does rotate across blocks (t0/t1/t2/t0/t1, confirmed in tallTown.terraceTints) and is visible as a color-temperature shift block to block, but nothing in the silhouette reads as elevation/height. 08 (1:1 close-up on the block0/block1 boundary) confirms why: the earth cross-section is present but reads as a thin, low-contrast strip right against the road bar, easy to miss and not readable as a cliff face. The silhouette edge-cut (up to 12px bleed) is too small relative to tile size (52px) to register as an irregular block outline at either zoom level.
tallTownVisualJudgement.highestLeverageFix: Deepen and darken the earth cross-section — TERRACE_EARTH_PX (currently 10px, townLayout.ts) is the ONE element that specifically encodes 'this is a vertical drop' rather than just 'this is a different color zone'; the tint rotation alone reads as zoning, not elevation. Roughly double the height and increase the --terrace-earth/--terrace-earth-dk contrast against the plateau tints (App.css) before touching tint contrast or silhouette-cut magnitude — those help but don't fix the core 'no visible height change' read on their own.
tallTownVisualJudgement.notImplemented: Diagnosis only, per instruction — no CSS/townLayout.ts changes made.
